instruction: In the container, repository at /gin (a Go project). Read the file /gin/render/json.go and report its complete verbatim content, plus the content of any file that defines WriteJSON (search for `func WriteJSON` under /gin). Do NOT edit anything. Report exact code snippets.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project). Read /gin/binding/multipart_form_mapping.go and report its complete verbatim content. Also report the content of /gin/binding/multipart_form_mapping_test.go if it exists, and any test files under /gin/binding that test setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles (grep -rn setArrayOfMultipartFormFiles /gin). Do NOT edit anything. Report exact code snippets verbatim.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project). Read /gin/binding/form_mapping.go and report verbatim the full implementation of setFormMap (and any helper it calls, e.g. mapUri/mapForm/trySetMap etc.). Specifically answer: when the destination is a map[string]string and a form key has multiple values (e.g. ?foo=a&foo=b), which value ends up stored — the first or the last? Show the exact code lines that decide this, with line numbers. Also report the content of /gin/binding/form_mapping_test.go tests that cover map[string]string with multiple values (e.g. TestMappingFormStringMap or similar), verbatim. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). Read /gin/mode.go and report verbatim the full SetMode function and the surrounding constants/vars (ginMode, Mode, debugPrintRouteFunc, envGinMode etc.). Answer precisely: what does SetMode do when passed an empty string ("") and the "test.v" flag is NOT present (i.e. flag.Lookup("test.v") == nil)? Show the exact code path with line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, the repository is checked out at /gin. Investigate the file(s) named errors.go in /gin (use `find /gin -name errors.go`). Report: (1) the full path(s) of errors.go; (2) the complete content of the relevant errors.go file(s); (3) what the Go package is and what the module is (cat go.mod); (4) any error types defined there and whether they implement an Unwrap() method, and whether the Unwrap implementation looks wrong (e.g. returns wrong type, wrong field, infinite recursion, returns nil incorrectly, uses value receiver vs pointer receiver mismatch, etc.). Do NOT edit any files. Just report findings verbatim with code snippets.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). Read /gin/recovery.go and report verbatim the `source` function (and the helper it uses, e.g. `func source(lines []string, n int) (src string)`). Answer precisely: what does source(lines, n) return when n < 0 or when n >= len(lines)? Show the exact code with line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, module github.com/gin-gonic/gin). Do NOT modify anything in /gin. TASK: produce a byte-exact, independent dump of /gin/errors.go and its test file, and report verbatim. Steps: (1) `cd /gin && md5sum errors.go && wc -l errors.go && cat -A errors.go` (cat -A reveals tabs/hidden chars); (2) `cd /gin && cat errors_test.go` (full file, verbatim); (3) `cd /gin && grep -rn 'Unwrap' --include=*.go .` and report all hits; (4) `cd /gin && git log --all --oneline && git stash list && git diff baseline --stat && git show baseline:errors.go | md5sum && git show HEAD:errors.go | md5sum`; (5) `cd /gin && grep -rn 'func (msg \*Error)' errors.go` and list every method with its receiver type and line number. Report everything verbatim, no edits, no summary-only: I need the raw text.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). Read /gin/binding/default_validator.go and report it verbatim. Answer precisely: what tag name does defaultValidator.lazyinit set on the validator (look for v.SetTagName(...) and the surrounding constants)? Show the exact code with line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). Read /gin/recovery.go and report verbatim the `defaultHandleRecovery` function (and any related function it calls, e.g. AbortWithStatus / AbortWithError in context.go). Answer precisely: what does defaultHandleRecovery do when called (what status code does it set, does it abort, does it write a body, does it log)? Show exact code with line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). Read /gin/binding/form_mapping.go and report verbatim the setTimeField function (and the constants it uses, e.g. timeFormats / timeFormatISO8601 etc., wherever they are defined — grep for them). Answer precisely: when the field's `time_format` tag is empty, which time format(s) does setTimeField try, and in what order? Show exact code with line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project). Investigate /gin/response_writer.go. Steps: (1) `cat /gin/response_writer.go` and report it verbatim; (2) `grep -rn "StatusCode" /gin --include=*.go` and report relevant lines; (3) look at /gin/response_writer_test.go and report the tests that exist (especially anything named TestResponseWriterStatusCode or similar); (4) reason about what the expected behavior of the StatusCode() method should be (per the file's doc comments) versus what the code does, e.g. does it return the wrong field, forget to handle the case where WriteHeader was never called, return 0 instead of 200, return the wrong value after Write() implicitly writes 200, etc. Report your conclusion with exact code snippets and line numbers. Do NOT edit any files.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin, module github.com/gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX a bug in /gin/errors.go. A hidden test named TestErrorUnwrap (in package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it tests the Unwrap() behavior of gin's error types (ErrorType/Error/ErrorChain, e.g. errors.Unwrap on an Error/ErrorChain should return the wrapped error, and errors.Is/As should work). Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` and record the baseline; (2) run `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -50` and record which tests fail BEFORE your change (these are the only tests allowed to fail); (3) read /gin/errors.go fully and find the divergence from its documented behavior (doc comments in that file are the contract). Likely bug: an Unwrap method returning the wrong thing (e.g. returning the receiver, returning nil always, wrong field, missing method, or pointer/value receiver mismatch). (4) Fix it minimally, in place, only in /gin/errors.go (do not touch tests). (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` and also write a TEMPORARY test in /tmp (not in the repo) or use a small throwaway program under /tmp to check that errors.Unwrap/errors.Is behave correctly on gin.Error and gin.ErrorChain. Delete any temp files you create inside /gin. Report: the exact diff you applied, the before/after test results, and confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). QUICK read-only status check (do NOT edit anything): (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain && git diff` and report the full diff; (2) `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -20` and report results; (3) `cd /gin && grep -n 'func (msg' errors.go | head -20` and `grep -n 'return' response_writer.go | head -20`; (4) `cd /gin && grep -n 'func (w \*responseWriter) WriteHeader' -A 10 response_writer.go`. Report everything verbatim and concisely.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX a bug in /gin/tree.go. A hidden test named TestRouteParamsNotEmpty (in package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it likely checks that route params (c.Params) are non-empty / that a wildcard or param route matches correctly and does not produce an empty param value, or that a path like "/" or a trailing-slash / catch-all route does not yield an empty param. Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` (record baseline); (2) run `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests fail BEFORE any change (only these may fail afterwards); (3) read /gin/tree.go fully and compare against its documented behavior in comments and against /gin/tree_test.go expectations; look for logic errors in insertChild / addRoute / getValue / findCaseInsensitivePath / countParams / countSections / wildcard handling, e.g. off-by-one, wrong comparison, wrong variable used, missing break, wrong index, inverted condition, wrong slice bound. (4) Fix minimally in /gin/tree.go only. Do NOT modify any test file. (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`; also `go test -run 'TestTree|TestRoute' -v ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`. Additionally write a throwaway test OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp) or a small program to check that params from routes like /user/:name, /user/*action, and paths with empty-ish segments behave sensibly. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, and confirmation no previously-passing test now fails.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). URGENT TASK: find and FIX a bug in the function `findCaseInsensitivePath` in /gin/tree.go (and any helper it calls, e.g. findCaseInsensitivePathRec). A hidden test named TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard (package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it tests that FindCaseInsensitivePath works when a node has multiple children AND a wildcard/catch-all child (e.g. routes /foo/bar, /foo/baz, /foo/*wildcard or similar) — likely the wildcard child is skipped/ignored or the wrong child is chosen, or the returned ciPath is wrong. Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` (record baseline); (2) `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests fail BEFORE any change (only these may fail afterwards); (3) read /gin/tree.go fully, especially findCaseInsensitivePathRec, and compare against the documented behavior in comments and against existing tests in /gin/tree_test.go (grep for FindCaseInsensitivePath tests). Look for logic errors: wrong comparison, missing wildcard branch, wrong index/offset, wrong slice bound, inverted condition, off-by-one in the ciPath buffer, not handling the catchAll child. (4) Fix minimally in /gin/tree.go only, and ONLY in the findCaseInsensitivePath code path. IMPORTANT: another agent may be concurrently editing a DIFFERENT function in /gin/tree.go (route param handling); so re-read the file immediately before each edit and make surgical edits that do not touch other functions. Do NOT modify any test file. (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`, plus `go test -run 'FindCaseInsensitivePath' -v . 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also write a throwaway program under /tmp (NOT in /gin) that builds a gin router with multiple children plus a wildcard and calls FindCaseInsensitivePath with various cases to confirm correct behavior. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX a bug in /gin/context.go related to content negotiation. A hidden test named TestContextNegotiationFormat2 (package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it tests Context.Negotiate / NegotiateFormat behavior (Accept header parsing, MIME type matching, wildcards like */* or application/*, quality values, and the fallback to the first offered format). Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` (record baseline); (2) `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests fail BEFORE any change (only these may fail afterwards); (3) read /gin/context.go, focusing on Negotiate, NegotiateFormat, and the helper that parses the Accept header (e.g. parseAccept / acceptSlice / accept), and compare against the documented behavior in the doc comments and against /gin/context_test.go (grep for Negotiation tests: TestContextNegotiationFormat, TestContextNegotiationFormatWithAccept, TestContextNegotiationFormatCustom, TestContextNegotiationFormatWithAcceptAndMimeType, etc.) and /gin/internal/... if relevant. Look for logic errors: wrong index, inverted condition, wrong comparison (e.g. using < instead of >), off-by-one, wrong slice bound, wrong variable, missing wildcard handling, wrong quality ordering. (4) Fix minimally in /gin/context.go only. IMPORTANT: other agents may be concurrently editing OTHER files (errors.go, tree.go, response_writer.go); do NOT touch those files, and re-read context.go immediately before each edit. Do NOT modify any test file. (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and `go test -run 'Negotiat' -v . 2>&1 | tail -60`. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. under /tmp with a module that has `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`) exercising NegotiateFormat with various Accept headers (including `*/*`, `application/*`, `text/html;q=0.9`, no Accept header, and unmatched types) and report the outputs. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, and confirmation no previously-passing test now fails.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX a bug in /gin/response_writer.go. A hidden test named TestResponseWriterStatusCode (package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it tests the status code reported by the response writer, e.g. that after WriteHeader(404) the writer's Status() is 404, that after Write() without WriteHeader it is 200, that WriteHeaderNow flushes the right code, that Size()/Written() are right, and that a status of 0 (never written) is reported as 200 (or that the default status is 200). Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` (record baseline); (2) `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests fail BEFORE any change (only these may fail afterwards); (3) read /gin/response_writer.go fully and compare against the doc comments in that file and against /gin/response_writer_test.go (report what those tests assert); look for logic errors: wrong field returned by Status(), wrong default status, WriteHeader not storing the code, WriteHeaderNow writing the wrong code, Written() checking the wrong field, size accounting, wrong comparison/condition, missing initialization. (4) Fix minimally in /gin/response_writer.go only. IMPORTANT: other agents are concurrently editing OTHER files (errors.go, tree.go, context.go); do NOT touch those files, and re-read response_writer.go immediately before editing. Do NOT modify any test file. (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and `go test -run 'ResponseWriter|Status' -v . 2>&1 | tail -60`. Also write a throwaway program under /tmp (NOT in /gin, own module with `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`) that uses httptest to exercise: no write at all, Write only, WriteHeader(404) only, WriteHeader(404) then Write, Write then WriteHeader(404), and report Status()/Size()/Written() in each case. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, and confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.

In the container, repository at /gin (Go project, gin-gonic/gin). TASK: find and FIX a bug in /gin/context.go related to the Attachment / Content-Disposition filename. A hidden test named TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment (package gin) is expected to pass after the fix; it likely checks that Context.Attachment(filename, ...) correctly escapes/sanitises the filename in the Content-Disposition header (e.g. using url.PathEscape or url.QueryEscape, and handling a filename containing non-ASCII characters or a path separator like "/" or "\\" — a common gin behavior is to take only the base name and to escape it). Steps: (1) `cd /gin && git status --porcelain` (record baseline; note another agent may be concurrently editing a DIFFERENT function in context.go — the content-negotiation code, Negotiate/NegotiateFormat — so DO NOT touch that code); (2) `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and record which tests fail BEFORE any change (only these may fail afterwards); (3) read the Attachment function in /gin/context.go and compare against its doc comment and against the existing tests in /gin/context_test.go (grep -n 'Attachment' /gin/context_test.go and report those tests verbatim). Look for logic errors: missing escaping of the filename, wrong escaping function (e.g. QueryEscape vs PathEscape), not using filepath.Base, wrong header format, inverted condition, wrong variable. (4) Fix minimally in /gin/context.go ONLY inside the Attachment function. Re-read the file immediately before editing and make a surgical edit so you do not clobber concurrent changes elsewhere in the file; after editing, run `cd /gin && git diff -- context.go` and confirm your change is the only one you made (other agents' changes may also appear — that is fine, just do not revert them). Do NOT modify any test file. (5) Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and `go test -run 'Attachment' -v . 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also write a throwaway program under /tmp (NOT in /gin, own module with `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`) that calls c.Attachment with filenames like "test.txt", "a/b.txt", "日本語.txt", "a b.txt" and prints the resulting Content-Disposition header. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, header outputs, and confirmation that no previously-passing test now fails.
